title: Three darknesses
hookLine: in the night, in the sea, inside the fish, Yunus calls out: there is no god but You, glory to You, I was wrong
tomorrow: the gourd and the saved city
last: WALKING AWAY IS ALSO A CHOICE.

cards: Have you ever been somewhere truly dark? The kind where you hold your hand in front of your face and see nothing. Now stack it.
It's night. Under the night, the sea. Under the sea, inside a great fish, a man.
Early commentators called it three darknesses: the dark of the night, the dark of the water, the dark of the belly of the fish. No ship, no crew, no one to hear him.
The man who walked out on his people in anger has nowhere left to walk. And in there, he says something.

teach.h: LA ILAHA ILLA ANTA: NO GOD BUT YOU.
teach.b: Surah Al-Anbiya says he cried out in the darkness, in Pickthall's translation: “There is no God save Thee. Be Thou glorified! Lo! I have been a wrong-doer.”
In Arabic: la ilaha illa anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu mina z-zalimin. Three short pieces. First, la ilaha illa anta: there is no god but You.
That's tawhid, day ten of this path, but said face to face. Not about Allah, to Him.
Second, subhanaka: glory to You, above any fault. Third, and hardest: I was one of the wrongdoers. No excuse.
He doesn't mention how stubborn his people were, or say they drove him to it.
He says, I was wrong. You've heard that shape before on this path. Adam and Hawwa: our Lord, we have wronged ourselves.
Musa after the blow: my Lord, I have wronged myself. The prophets keep saying it.

teach.h: WE HEARD HIS PRAYER AND SAVED HIM.
teach.b: Then the next verse: “Then We heard his prayer and saved him from the anguish. Thus We save believers.”
Not just Yunus: the Qur'an turns the story outward. A hadith in Tirmidhi says that whenever a Muslim calls with the prayer of Dhu n-Nun, for anything, it is answered.
That's why so many Muslims know these words by heart, and say them in their own dark places: a hospital corridor, a pile of debt, three in the morning.
Another surah adds that if Yunus had not been one who glorified Allah, he would have stayed in the belly of the fish until the day of rising.

how: Many Muslims say the prayer of Yunus, la ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu mina z-zalimin, in times of distress, sometimes repeating it many times, trusting the hadith that it is answered.

o: three lamps the sailors lit on deck
three sins Yunus confessed in the fish
the dark of night, sea and fish around Yunus

games.q: what's inside the prayer — tap the pairs.
p: there is no god but You
I was one of the wrongdoers

s: in the fish, Yunus blames his people for driving him away
he says only: I have been a wrong-doer (21:87).
the Qur'an says Allah saves believers the way He saved Yunus
then we heard his prayer and saved him from the anguish. thus we save believers (21:88).
the prayer of Yunus is only for prophets
a hadith in Tirmidhi says any Muslim who calls with it is answered.

games.q: Yunus is in the dark, inside the fish, with no one to hear. what does he say?
o: why did You let this happen to me?
there is no god but You, glory to You, I was wrong.
games.why: there is no God save Thee. be Thou glorified! lo! I have been a wrong-doer (21:87). and the next verse: we heard his prayer.

practice: Close your eyes and let it be dark. If you pray, say the prayer of Yunus slowly, three times, silently or in a whisper, with a breath between each piece: la ilaha illa anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu mina z-zalimin.
If you don't pray, simply listen to the words in your mind and let the last one land: I was wrong, said without an excuse.

wordCard.voice: Three darknesses. The night, the sea and the fish, where Yunus called: there is no god but You, glory to You, I was wrong.

orig.s: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
orig.say: laa i-LAA-ha il-LAA AN-ta, sub-HAA-na-ka, IN-nee KUN-tu mi-naz-zaa-li-MEEN
orig.note: Arabic, Qur'an 21:87: the prayer of Yunus in the dark.

carryVoice: Your line: la ilaha illa anta, there is no god but You. Tomorrow, what happened when he came out. See you then.
